Multi-School Management

Run every school in your group from one system.

Admissions, attendance, fees, exams and billing — with access decided by each school’s own plan.

Sign inSee what is included

Accounts are created by your administrator — there is no public sign-up.

Five people open this system, and each sees a different one.

Not one screen with things greyed out. Each role has its own navigation, its own dashboard, and a server that will not answer for anything outside its scope.

  • Group operators

    One platform console across every organisation and school: plans, subscriptions, invoices, payments and coupons in a single ledger.

  • School principals

    Admissions, staff, classes and sections, timetables, exams and fees for one school — scoped so no school can read another.

  • Teachers

    Attendance, marks, homework and the timetable, on the classes actually assigned to them.

  • Parents

    Each child’s attendance, results and fees, without an account per school.

  • Students

    Their own timetable, homework and results.

The parts that are hard to retrofit.

Tenancy, entitlements, billing and audit are decided at the boundary, so a new school is a row rather than a release.

  • Organisations, then schools

    A two-level tenancy. Every query is confined to the caller’s scope by the server, not by the screen asking politely.

  • Plans decide access

    What a school can open is its subscription’s entitlement snapshot — modules, feature flags and usage limits. Never a plan name hard-coded in a branch.

  • Billing that reconciles

    Subscriptions, proration, add-ons, coupons, quotations, invoices, payments and refunds — with a review step before money is recognised.

  • Reports built on the ledger

    Financial, fee-collection, expense, attendance and academic reports read the same rows the operational screens write.

  • An audit trail

    Writes record who changed what, before and after, with the reason given.

  • Configured, not customised

    Roles, permissions, grading scales, fee structures and school settings are data. Adding a school does not mean shipping code.

Twenty modules. A plan turns on the ones a school pays for.

This is the whole list, not a selection — the same keys the entitlement snapshot carries. A school that is not entitled to a module does not see it in its navigation, and its endpoints refuse.

Sixteen are built and in use today. Four are part of the catalogue and not yet implemented; they are marked below rather than left to look finished.
